_comment: Registry for tests/test_erasure_coverage.py (#856). The test runs the Worker migrations in an in-memory SQLite and reads the schema from it. Every table is listed with the exact column list it was judged on, a class and a reason; every view and trigger is listed under other_objects; reviewed_schema_digest pins the whole schema (types, defaults, keys, objects), so a changed column set or type fails the test until the entry is looked at again. The test cannot prove a person looked: a second human reviewer on any change to this file is a policy control (docs/privacy.md), not something CI enforces. classes: lead = rows that hold an address or carry a lead id, removed by `reach-around leads delete` (its SQL must delete the table and its read-back must count it); lead_hash = a keyed hash of an event that can include an address, short-lived, cleared whole and read back to 0 by `reach-around leads delete --finish` (the guard test runs that flow on seeded rows); a table the flow does not clear must be listed under known_gaps with an issue number that is itself listed under reviewed_issues with its title (adding either changes the registry digest; human review of that edit is a policy control), and a lead_hash entry needs a reason that names how the value is derived and its lifetime (40+ characters) and a reviewed reason for every column the vocabulary flags, the hash column included, or the test fails; erasure_claim_review lists the files that use an erasure word and make no complete-erasure claim (every other such file must name the manual alert step, #905; the public privacy page template names it as 'keyed hash' plus 'owner clears it manually' instead, since a visitor page cites no issue number); unlinkable = visitor rows with no address, no IP address and no lead id, so a request cannot be matched to them (Art. 11), bounded by retention; aggregate = counts, labels and bookkeeping with no row per person; internal = SQLite's own table. reviewed_columns: a column in a table that is not class lead whose name matches the test's personal-data vocabulary, or whose declared type is blob or none, or whose default is an expression, each with the reason it holds no personal data (at least 12 characters). backup: whether scripts/backup-d1.sh exports the table (never or exported); only checked for classes lead, lead_hash and unlinkable.

trigger.kit_meta_floor_insert: BEFORE INSERT guard that aborts a negative session floor; copies nothing and writes no row.
trigger.kit_meta_floor_update: BEFORE UPDATE guard that aborts a negative session floor; copies nothing and writes no row.

leads.reason: One row per address typed into the kit gate. Removed by the delete tool (id and address paired). Also purged by age (worker/src/kit/leadretention.ts).

kit_events.reason: Hour-rounded unlock, view and verify events keyed by lead_id. Removed by the delete tool; the foreign key cascades as a second layer.

alert_dedup.reason: HMAC of site, event kind and the event identity (an address, or the inquiry fields) under a secret key; a row stops counting as a repeat after 10 minutes (expires_at) but is deleted only when the next alert event is admitted (or when cleared), so on a quiet site it can stay stored indefinitely (at most 500 rows). The lead delete SQL does not touch it: `reach-around leads delete --finish` (#905) checks the schemas, confirms the lead rows are gone, clears the whole table and reads it back to 0 twice (docs/privacy.md, checklist item 7); a keyed hash is not treated as erased by being hard to match.

reviewed_columns.event_hash: the only hash column: a keyed HMAC of the event under a secret key, fixed-length hex text, never the address; the row expires after 10 minutes

visitor_seen.reason: Daily keyed hash of the connection address with no other column; deleted after its day. Holds no lead id and no address, so it cannot be joined to a lead.

reviewed_columns.h: keyed daily hash of the connection address, own table, no join key; removed within about an hour of the day ending

view_events.reason: Raw page view rows: coarse categories only, no address, user agent string, referrer URL or lead id. Retention purge removes them.

reviewed_columns.src_kind: closed one-letter source kind (direct, internal, referrer host, utm label, other)
reviewed_columns.src: referrer host or campaign label, not a URL
reviewed_columns.country: two-letter country code from the edge
reviewed_columns.region: coarse region name, default geo level
reviewed_columns.city: empty unless GEO_LEVEL=city; never joined to a person

click_events.reason: One row per accepted click: hour-rounded time, link id, source label. No address, user agent or referrer. Retention purge removes them.

reviewed_columns.country: two-letter country code; the Worker no longer writes it (migration 0010) and old rows age out
reviewed_columns.src: closed source label, never a URL or an address

alert_quota.reason: Per-minute and per-day alert counters by site and channel; no content.

analytics_coverage.reason: 24 letters per day saying whether collection ran.

click_budget_lh.reason: Hourly landing and hop write budget counters.

reviewed_columns.country: country code in an aggregate count
country code in an aggregate count

click_src_daily.reason: Daily click counts by source label.

reviewed_columns.src: closed source label in an aggregate count

click_src_monthly.reason: Monthly click counts by source label.

reviewed_columns.src: closed source label in an aggregate count

counters.reason: Route budgets and daily or hourly counters keyed by a short slug. Counts of gate events cannot be un-counted and are not personal data about one person.

db_identity.reason: One fixed role label (analytics) that lets the tools tell this database from the leads database; no row per person.

kit_meta.reason: Heartbeats and the unstored session floor: one integer per slug, no person.

reviewed_columns.value: STRICT INTEGER: a timestamp or counter per slug, cannot hold text

view_city_daily.reason: Daily view counts by city, only at GEO_LEVEL=city.

reviewed_columns.country: country code in an aggregate count
reviewed_columns.region: region name in an aggregate count
reviewed_columns.city: city name in an aggregate count, purged on its own window

view_daily.reason: Daily view counts by page and source.

reviewed_columns.src: source label in an aggregate count
reviewed_columns.country: country code in an aggregate count

view_dim_daily.reason: Daily view counts by one coarse dimension.

reviewed_columns.value: closed label of the coarse dimension (browser family, device class, language tag) in an aggregate count

reviewed_columns.country: country code in an aggregate count
reviewed_columns.region: region name in an aggregate count
reviewed_columns.city: city name in an aggregate count

view_meta.reason: Small key and value state: cursors, budgets, health flags. Never request data.

reviewed_columns.value: cursor, lease token, budget or health flag set by the Worker itself, never request data

view_rollup_log.reason: Rollup bookkeeping per site and day.

reviewed_columns.raw_views: integer count of raw rows rolled up that day, not the rows

sqlite_sequence.reason: SQLite's own autoincrement bookkeeping: table names and counters.

reviewed_columns.name: the name of one of our own tables, written by SQLite
reviewed_columns.seq: the last row id handed out for that table, an integer written by SQLite

runtime_stores._comment: Non-D1 places the Worker can write. The test lists every file under worker/src (any extension) that names a storage primitive (KV put, caches, R2, Durable Objects, queues, Analytics Engine, Vectorize, Hyperdrive, service bindings, a computed property or dynamic env access) or a storage binding found in every wrangler*.toml, wrangler*.json and wrangler*.jsonc file (commented templates included). This is a lexical inventory of where storage is named, not a proof of where data flows: a write that never names a primitive or a binding is not seen, and an operator must verify the deployed KV namespace by hand. A new mention fails the test until it is listed here with the reason it holds no lead data.

worker/src/live.ts.put: live poller token cache and state in LIVE_KV, plus the edge cache of the public status body: platform tokens and stream state, no visitor data
worker/src/live.ts.caches: edge cache of the public live status body, no visitor data
worker/src/live.ts.binding:LIVE_KV: the live status namespace: platform tokens and stream state only, no visitor data

worker/src/kit/env.ts.KVNamespace: type of the KIT binding; the Worker only reads the gated page from it (key kit/v1) and never writes it
worker/src/kit/env.ts.binding:KIT: type and presence check of the KIT binding, no write

worker/src/kit/gate.ts.binding:KIT: one read of the gated page (env.KIT.get), never a write

worker/src/index.ts.binding:KIT: type-level pass-through of the KIT binding in the Worker env, no read or write

worker/src/kit/budgetcheck.ts.dynamic-env: reads a closed list of setting names from a plain string map in the deploy check, not a storage binding

reviewed_call_sites._comment: For every file and primitive above: a short hash of each statement (comments and spacing removed, the whole call including its arguments) that mentions the primitive, h*N when the same statement appears N times, or comment when it is only named in comments. A new call through an approved primitive or binding, or an edit to a reviewed one, changes the list and fails the test until a person has read what it writes and recorded the new hash. It pins statement text, not data flow.

export_paths._comment: Every place that can read the database out. A file over 2 MB is scanned in chunks; one over 64 MB is not read and must be listed under unscanned_large_files with a reason (a lockfile or snapshot, for example), or the test fails by name. commands: every text file in the repository outside dependency and cache directories and Markdown (shell scripts anywhere, every package.json, Makefile and justfile, workflows and composite actions, Containerfile, deploy files, JSON and YAML command arrays, tests, the CLI) that contains a wrangler d1 export, execute or time-travel call or a dump tool, also when the words are split across quoted array items, list items or a line continuation (found by scanning; a new one fails the test; JSON is parsed and keys starting with an underscore are ignored). whole_database_docs: Markdown that shows a wrangler d1 export with no --table, which dumps every table including the lead tables. backup_extra_tables: tables backup-d1.sh exports that no migration creates. The backup script itself is also run against a recording stub in the test and every wrangler call it makes is judged against the store classes.

commands.scripts/backup-d1.sh: The only exporter. One named table per export call, from a fixed list; its one other call is the table listing. The test runs it against a recording stub and rejects any call that names a lead or never-exported table, a whole-database export or a different query.
commands.scripts/check-dump.py: Reads a dump and refuses addresses; the match is a docstring mention of the export command, it never makes a dump.
commands.scripts/erasure-stores.json: This registry: its prose names the export commands it inventories; it runs nothing.
commands.tests/test_backup_d1.py: Test fixtures: a stub wrangler records the backup script's calls; no real database is read.
commands.tests/test_check_dump.py: Test fixtures for the dump checker; synthetic text only, no export is made.
commands.tests/test_erasure_coverage.py: This test: command strings in hostile fixtures and a recording stub; nothing runs against a real database.
commands.tests/test_leads_delete.py: Test fixtures for the delete tool's `d1 execute` text, run against a stub; no real database is read.
commands.tests/test_leads_show.py: Test fixtures for the lead lookup's `d1 execute` text, run against a stub; no real database is read.
commands.worker/migrations/0007_rollup_max_id.sql: A comment in a migration that mentions the export command; the SQL runs no export.
commands.scripts/clear-click-country.sh: Counts and clears the retired country column of click_events and counts two aggregate tables; reads no lead table and writes no file.
commands.src/reach_around/commands/leads.py: The erasure tool itself: its `d1 execute` text is the owner-run delete and read-back SQL for the lead tables, and it reads the lead list the owner exports by hand (checklist item 5).
commands.src/reach_around/funnel/export.py: Reads a d1 execute JSON file the owner supplies for aggregate reports; a docstring mention, it runs nothing.

whole_database_docs.docs/deploy.md: Tells the owner to export before a migration (a hand-made whole-database dump that includes lead tables); checklist item 5 covers deleting it.
whole_database_docs.docs/failure-modes.md: Backstop export before schema changes: a hand-made whole-database dump that includes lead tables; checklist item 5 covers deleting it.
whole_database_docs.docs/wiki/deploy/06-updating.md: Backstop export before an update: a hand-made whole-database dump that includes lead tables; checklist item 5 covers deleting it.

backup_extra_tables.d1_migrations: Wrangler's own migration history: file names and apply times, no person.
